parameters, energy carriers used, production process, age of machines and equipment,
location and environmental conditions, and business conditions, their determination at the
NACE level can have some issue.

deviation from benchmark.

study_limitations.evidence_quote:
a numeric threshold of sites was set, conventionally equal to 5, below which
the modelling was not carried out because the sample would not be statistically representa-
tive.

The information for second-level EnPIs is
scarce, but the obtained electrical EnPI
values for raw-material preparation, solid-fuel preparation, ﬁnish grinding, and clinker
cooking are slightly higher than the best available technologies (BAT) [54] and lower than
the values for the U.S. as of 1999 [55].

However, a high heterogeneity of the available data has been
observed, as in the methodology used in the analysis and in the obtained results.

reviewer_notes: The paper presents a sectoral methodology applied to the Italian cement industry (NACE 23.51, complete grey-cement production cycle, 29 sites). For each energy vector it reports both a mean SEC (real EnPI ± SD, reliability class) and a linear regression of absolute energy consumption on production, from which a hyperbolic EnPIm is derived; these are recorded as separate models (M1-M3 mean SEC; M4-M6 first-level regressions; M7-M10 second-level phase regressions; M11 thermal EnPI segmented by number of cyclones). The regression 'metrics' are recorded as in-sample fit. Section 4.4 (Table 6) validates the first-level EnPIs by comparison with external published benchmarks (BREF, IEA, UNIDO etc.); this is an external benchmark comparison rather than a held-out/statistical out-of-sample validation, so out_of_sample_validation is coded not reported for all models — reviewer may wish to reconsider. Estimation method (OLS) is never explicitly stated, hence not reported. Energy-savings results are described qualitatively for the EE audit database in general but not tied to specific models, so energy_result is not applicable per model.
